Once again, on its traditional dates in early December, the Gran Hotel Bali in Benidorm opens its doors to host this traditional, well-attended, and international Chess Festival, which began in 2002. This year marks its 23rd edition.

Undoubtedly, the International Chess Open - Group A continues to improve its commitment to excellence each year. The International Amateur Grand Tournament - Group B continues to offer a substantial prize fund, perhaps one of the highest in the world for players rated under 2000 Elo.

tour.name: 2026/27 U.S. National Collegiate Women's Individual Championship
tour.description:
## 2026-27 U.S. National Collegiate Women's Individual Championship

**November 14-15, 2026** · 9-round Swiss · G/20+10 · Free · Online on Lichess

 **Official website:** https://uswc.chess.stream/
 **Register / Entries:** https://uswc.chess.stream/register
 **Pairings:** https://uswc.chess.stream/pairings
 **Standings:** https://uswc.chess.stream/standings
 **Team Standings:** https://uswc.chess.stream/teamstanding

---

##  Schedule (Central Time)

**Saturday, November 14**
- 10:00 AM CST: Registration closes
- 11:00 AM CST: **Round 1**
- 12:15 PM CST: **Round 2**
- 1:30 PM CST: **Round 3**
- 2:45 PM CST: **Round 4**
- 4:00 PM CST: **Round 5**

**Sunday, November 15**
- 11:00 AM CST: **Round 6**
- 12:15 PM CST: **Round 7**
- 1:30 PM CST: **Round 8**
- 2:45 PM CST: **Round 9**

---

# Regulations

## 1. Registration
- **1A.** The 2026-27 U.S. National Collegiate Women's Individual Championship is a free event - there is no entry fee.
- **1B.** All registration is online through this website. Registration closes 1 hour before round 1.
- **1C.** College students must register using their official academic institution email address.
- **1D.** There is no limit to the number of participants per college.

## 2. Eligibility
- **2A.** Only students of Accredited Postsecondary Education Institutions and Programs listed by the US Department of Education are eligible to compete.
- **2B.** A player must be listed as a female in their US Chess record.
- **2C.** An active US Chess membership is required. Foreign GM/WGM/IM/WIM are exempted from the requirement.
- **2D.** Players who hold a title of GM/IM/WGM/WIM shall be full-time degree seeking students. In the final semester of their degree program, the players can be enrolled in fewer classes if it suffices to complete their degree requirements.
- **2E.** Students enrolled in high school, even those who are taking college courses as part of a "dual enrollment" program, are not eligible to compete.
- **2F.** Faculty and staff are not eligible to compete. In this context, the term "faculty and staff" does not include student employees.
- **2G.** A student is eligible to compete in the cycle in at most 6 distinct academic years.

## 3. Ratings
- **3A.** US Chess OTB Regular Ratings shall be used for pairing purposes.
- **3B.** Players without US Chess OTB Regular Ratings shall have their FIDE Standard Rating converted for tournament purposes:
  - US Chess = FIDE × 0.564 + 932, if their FIDE Regular Rating is lower than 2000
  - US Chess = FIDE × 1.02 + 20, if their FIDE Regular Rating is at least 2000
- **3C.** Players without US Chess OTB Regular and FIDE Standard Ratings shall be considered unrated.
- **3D.** The tournament will be rated by US Chess for Online Regular Rating.

## 4. Format and Pairings
- **4A.** The championship is a 9-round Swiss System individual online tournament.
- **4B.** Players from the same college shall not be paired against each other in any round.
- **4C.** The time control is game in 20 minutes, with a 10-second increment from move one.
- **4D.** Players can take as many zero-point byes as they wish, but they shall request it before registration closes (one hour before the start of the championship).
- **4E.** Players who do not show up in time to make their first move before they run out of time will be forfeited and removed from the tournament, unless the Chief Arbiter decides otherwise.

## 5. Scoring and Prizes
- **5A.** An individual (game) win is worth 1 point, a draw is worth ½ point, and a loss is worth 0 points.
- **5B.** The top player shall be declared the 2026-27 U.S. National Collegiate Women's Individual Champion.
- **5C.** In the event of a tie for first place, the players shall be declared co-champions.
- **5D.** Additional champions will be crowned for: U2200, U2000, U1800, U1600, U1400, U1200, and U1000/Unrated.
- **5E.** The top four colleges in the Team Standings will qualify for the 2026-27 Women's President's Cup.
- **5F.** Team standings are determined by the sum of the top four individual scores from the college.

## 6. Schedule
See the schedule at the top of this page (Central Time).

## 7. Technical Requirements
- **7A.** Players are required to be on a video call via Zoom during the championship.
- **7B.** The Zoom link will be e-mailed to all the participants before the start of the first round.
- **7C.** Players are required to share their screen with the Zoom call.
- **7D.** Players are not allowed to use virtual background.
- **7E.** Players shall have their microphones off.
- **7F.** Players without a camera, or refusing to turn it on, will be forfeited for that round unless the Chief Arbiter decides otherwise.
- **7G.** Players shall remain in front of the camera during the game. Players that go off-camera may be forfeited for that round.
- **7H.** Players are required to move their webcam to show the Chief Arbiter their playing area upon request.
- **7I.** Zoom monitoring sessions, including video or/and audio, may be recorded for the purpose of ensuring fair play.

## 8. Disconnections and Technical Issues
- **8A.** A short disconnect may keep the clock running. A longer disconnect will result in a forfeit.
- **8B.** It is every player's individual responsibility to have:
  - Working playing device
  - Working camera
  - Working microphone
  - Stable Internet connection
  - Account created and verified on the playing platform
  - Knowledge and experience how to play on the playing platform

## 9. Fair Play
- **9A.** Outside assistance of any kind is strictly prohibited.
- **9B.** Headphones, earphones and any kind of audio device or electronic devices not used for playing are not allowed during the rounds.
- **9C.** No spectators are allowed in the playing area.
- **9D.** No other software shall be running during games besides: Operating System, Antivirus, Zoom, Web browser that is connecting to the playing platform, and Software needed to make the camera and microphone work.
- **9E.** Players shall obey the Terms of Service of the playing platform.
- **9F.** A fair play violation may potentially lead to severe punishments, including: Warning, Forfeit of a single game, Expulsion from the championship, or Other penalties the Chief Arbiter deems adequate.
- **9G.** Upon the completion of the last round of the championship, the Chief Arbiter will be given 2 weeks to analyze fair play data. This time can be extended, if deemed necessary.
- **9H.** Serious Fair Play violations might be communicated to FIDE Fair Play Commission, US Chess Ethics Committee, and/or college authorities.

## 10. Tiebreaks
For sole purpose of determining places and rating category champions, the following tie-breaking systems will be used:
1. Solkoff
2. Cumulative
3. Cumulative of Opposition
4. Coin Toss

Sonntag, 29. November 2026 | Beginn 12:00 Uhr

Schach trifft auf Geschichte! Im prachtvollen Marmorsaal des Stiftes Dürnstein, mitten im Weltkulturerbe Wachau, geht das 4. Internationale Dürnstein Open in seine zweite Runde.

Nach dem Blitzturnier am Samstag steht der Sonntag ganz im Zeichen des Schnellschachs. Sieben spannende Runden im Schweizer System mit einer Bedenkzeit von 12 Minuten + 5 Sekunden pro Zug versprechen packende Duelle, überraschende Wendungen und hochklassiges Schach in einer der außergewöhnlichsten Turnierlocations Österreichs.

Schach im Turm bringt die Spitzenbretter live zu euch nach Hause! Dank moderner DGT-Technik können die Partien hier auf Lichess Zug um Zug mitverfolgt werden. Begleitende Kamerabilder, Interviews und Kommentare aus dem historischen Marmorsaal machen das Schachwochenende auch für alle Daheimgebliebenen zu einem besonderen Erlebnis.

Wir wünschen allen Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern spannende Partien und unserem Publikum viel Vergnügen beim Mitfiebern!

tour.description:
TORNEO BRINGAS CHESS MONTERREY 2026

¡Ajedrez en el Corazón del Norte! ️

El Torneo Bringas Chess Monterrey 2026 es un evento de ajedrez rápido que busca consolidarse como un referente del ajedrez competitivo en el norte de México, reuniendo a jugadores de diferentes edades y niveles en un ambiente de sana competencia, convivencia y pasión por el deporte ciencia.

Se celebrará el domingo 15 de noviembre de 2026, a partir de las 10:00 horas, en el Salón Galería del Hotel Galería Plaza Monterrey, ubicado en el centro de la ciudad, en instalaciones cómodas, modernas y de fácil acceso.

 $60,000 en premios en efectivo y especie.

El torneo contará con cuatro categorías: Libre, Sub 20, Sub 16 y Sub 12, bajo el sistema suizo a cinco rondas, con un ritmo de juego de 10 minutos más 5 segundos de incremento por jugada.

Los participantes disfrutarán de excelentes condiciones de juego, con tableros, piezas y relojes en todas las mesas. Los primeros tres tableros de cada categoría serán electrónicos, permitiendo la transmisión de partidas en vivo por Internet.

Además de una atractiva premiación, se entregarán trofeos y medallas conmemorativas de diseño especial, así como un diploma personalizado a todos los participantes.

Bringas Chess apuesta por la calidad organizativa, la innovación tecnológica y el desarrollo de nuevos talentos, especialmente entre niños y jóvenes, promoviendo el ajedrez como una herramienta de formación, disciplina y convivencia.

 Sede: Hotel Galería Plaza Monterrey, Salón Galería.

 Fecha: 15 de noviembre de 2026.

 Informes e inscripciones: 618-165-53-21.

¡Monterrey nos espera para vivir una gran fiesta del ajedrez!
